title: Effective vs Ineffective Application Language
about: How to word each section so the court understands it
content:
Effective vs Ineffective Protection Order Application Language

Section 5: Acts of Domestic Violence Examples

Physical Abuse

WEAK: "He hurts me and makes me scared."

STRONG: "On 15 January 2025 at approximately 9pm at our shared residence in Wynberg, respondent grabbed my arm and twisted it, leaving visible bruises. He shouted 'I will kill you if you leave me.' This pattern has escalated over 6 months from verbal threats to physical violence."

WEAK: "My boyfriend hits me sometimes."

STRONG: "On 3 February 2025 at 7:30pm, respondent struck me three times across the face with his open hand after I asked where he had been. The blows left red marks and caused my lip to bleed. I sought medical treatment at Groote Schuur Hospital emergency room where Dr. Smith documented the injuries. This was the fourth physical assault in two months, with each incident more severe than the last."

Emotional/Psychological Abuse

WEAK: "He is controlling and jealous."

STRONG: "Respondent monitors all my phone calls and demands my passwords for WhatsApp and Facebook. On 20 January 2025, he destroyed my cell phone by throwing it against the wall because my sister called me. He regularly tells me 'You're worthless, no one else would want you' and has forbidden me from seeing my family for the past eight months. When I tried to visit my mother on 25 January 2025, he threatened to 'make me pay' if I left the house."

Economic Abuse

WEAK: "He controls our money."

STRONG: "Respondent took my bank card on 10 December 2024 and changed my PIN without my consent. He gives me only R50 per week for groceries for myself and our two children, while spending hundreds on alcohol for himself. He forced me to resign from my job at Pick n Pay in November 2024 by threatening to 'destroy' my workplace if I continued working. I have no access to money for basic necessities like children's school fees or medical expenses."

Threats and Intimidation

WEAK: "He threatens me."

STRONG: "On 28 January 2025 at 11pm, respondent held a kitchen knife to my throat and stated 'I will cut you open if you ever try to leave me.' He owns a licensed firearm which he showed me on 2 February 2025 while saying 'This bullet has your name on it.' These death threats occur weekly and have increased in frequency since I mentioned wanting to end our relationship in December 2024."

Sexual Abuse

WEAK: "He forces me to have sex."

STRONG: "On 5 February 2025, respondent forced me to have sexual intercourse against my will after I refused. When I resisted, he held me down and said 'You belong to me.' This has occurred approximately twice per week for the past three months. He also forces me to perform sexual acts that I find degrading and painful, threatening to hurt our children if I refuse."

Digital/Electronic Harassment

WEAK: "He bothers me on my phone."

STRONG: "Since our breakup on 15 January 2025, respondent sends me 20-30 WhatsApp messages daily, including photos of our house and my car, showing he is watching me. He has created fake Instagram accounts to follow my social media after I blocked his real account. On 1 February 2025, he sent a message stating 'I know you were at Woolworths at 2pm today, I'm always watching.' He has also posted intimate photos of me on social media without my consent."

Child Exposure

WEAK: "The children see us fight."

STRONG: "Our 6-year-old daughter Nomsa witnessed respondent slap me on 30 January 2025 and began crying hysterically. She has started wetting her bed and refuses to sleep alone since this incident. Our 10-year-old son Thabo tries to protect me during arguments and respondent has threatened to 'beat him like a man' if he interferes. Both children's school performance has declined and their teacher has noted behavioral changes since the domestic violence escalated in December 2024."

Section 6: Urgency Examples

Escalation Patterns

WEAK: "Things are getting worse."

STRONG: "The frequency and severity of respondent's violence has increased dramatically. In October 2024, incidents occurred monthly and involved only pushing. By December 2024, physical assaults occurred weekly and included hitting. Since January 2025, violence occurs almost daily and now includes threats with weapons. The most recent incident on 5 February 2025 was the most severe to date, involving strangulation until I nearly lost consciousness."

Immediate Threats

WEAK: "I'm scared something bad will happen."

STRONG: "Respondent has threatened to kill me if I seek help from the police or courts. On 4 February 2025, he said 'If you get a protection order against me, you'll be dead before the ink is dry.' He has easy access to our shared residence where I am alone with our children every evening. He knows my daily routine and work schedule, making it impossible for me to avoid contact without court intervention."

Weapon Access

WEAK: "He has dangerous things."

STRONG: "Respondent owns a licensed 9mm pistol which he keeps loaded in our bedroom. On 3 February 2025, he pointed it at my head and said 'One day I'm going to use this.' He also has a collection of hunting knives which he has used to threaten me on multiple occasions. Given his escalating violence and easy access to lethal weapons, I fear he will seriously injure or kill me without immediate court intervention."

Section 7: Terms of Protection Order Examples

Residence Restrictions

WEAK: "Don't let him come to my house."

STRONG: "Respondent must not enter the shared residence located at 25 Victoria Street, Wynberg, Cape Town, where I live with our two minor children. He must also be prohibited from coming within 100 meters of this property, as he has previously waited outside and followed me when I leave."

Workplace Protection

WEAK: "Keep him away from my work."

STRONG: "Respondent must not enter or come within 200 meters of my workplace at Shoprite, Claremont Centre, Main Road, Claremont, Cape Town. He has previously caused disturbances at my workplace on 20 January 2025, shouting at customers and threatening my manager when she asked him to leave."

Communication Restrictions

WEAK: "Stop him from contacting me."

STRONG: "Respondent must be prohibited from contacting me through any means including telephone, SMS, WhatsApp, social media, email, or through third parties. He must also be prohibited from creating fake social media accounts to monitor or contact me, as he has done previously after being blocked."

Section 8: Additional Conditions Examples

Weapon Seizure

WEAK: "Take his gun away."

STRONG: "SAPS must seize respondent's licensed 9mm pistol (license number [if known]) and all ammunition, as well as his collection of hunting knives kept at our shared residence. Given his repeated threats to kill me with these weapons and his escalating violence, continued possession poses an immediate threat to my life."

Emergency Monetary Relief

WEAK: "Make him pay for things."

STRONG: "Respondent must pay emergency monetary relief of R2,500 per month for rent and utilities for our shared residence, and R1,500 per month for our children's school fees and basic necessities. This relief is necessary because he forced me to resign from my employment and I have no current income to support myself and our children."

Property Collection

WEAK: "Help me get my stuff."

STRONG: "SAPS must accompany me to collect my personal belongings from our shared residence at 25 Victoria Street, Wynberg, including my clothing, identity documents, children's belongings, and my laptop computer which I need for work. Given respondent's violent threats when I previously tried to collect belongings, police escort is essential for my safety."

Key Principles for Effective Language

Always Include:

-   Specific dates and times: "On 15 January 2025 at approximately 9pm"

-   Exact locations: "at our shared residence in Wynberg"

-   Concrete actions: "grabbed my arm and twisted it"

-   Physical evidence: "leaving visible bruises"

-   Direct quotes of threats: "I will kill you if you leave me"

-   Pattern demonstration: "escalated over 6 months from verbal threats to physical violence"

Avoid Vague Language:

-   "Sometimes" → Use specific frequency: "twice per week"

-   "He hurts me" → Describe exact actions: "he struck me with his closed fist"

-   "I'm scared" → Explain specific fears: "I fear he will kill me based on his threats"

-   "Things are bad" → Detail specific incidents and escalation

Show Legal Understanding:

-   Connect incidents to legal definitions of domestic violence

-   Demonstrate understanding of urgency requirements

-   Link requested protections to specific abuse experienced

-   Show impact on children and other affected persons

Create Urgency:

-   Emphasize recent escalation in frequency or severity

-   Highlight immediate safety concerns

-   Detail access to weapons or means of harm

-   Show why delay in court action would increase danger
